Biography

Academic excellence with a practical edge

Thomas Kivevele holds a PhD and an M.Tech (cum laude) in Mechanical Engineering, focused on sustainable energy, from Tshwane University of Technology in Pretoria, and a B.Sc. (Hons) in Electro-Mechanical Engineering from the University of Dar es Salaam. In 2018 he received the Fulbright African Senior Research Scholar Award to research biofuels at Baylor University in Texas.

He joined NM-AIST as a Lecturer in February 2016 and became Associate Professor in 2023. He teaches renewable energy technologies, passive solar energy systems, refrigeration and air conditioning, and energy auditing and management. He leads the Clean Energy Technologies Research Group and the Sustainable Energy Lab, and served six years on the University Tender Board.

His work spans energy research programmes supported by the World Bank, the European Union and other partners. This site lists 116 journal articles and six registered patents covering solar dryers, a solar vaccine cooler and a biogas burner assembly. He was named NM-AIST's Best Innovator of the Year for 2020/21 and Best Worker of 2019/2020 among academic staff.

His consultancies include energy-efficient irrigation for the Tanzania Horticultural Association, a bio-digester and wetland for the Lake Victoria Environmental Management Programme, the 2024 Africa Energy Market Place for the African Development Bank, and waste-to-energy and rice husk valorisation projects for UNIDO.
